Mohar Singh Kuwhah vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh on 16
April, 2024
Author: Rohit Arya

Bench: Rohit Arya
 1
 In The High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Gwalior

 (Mohar Singh Kuwhah And Others Vs The State Of Madhya Pradesh)
Dated : 16-04-2024
 Shri Deependra Singh Raghuwanshi-Advocate for the appellant.
 Shri A.K. Nirankari-Public Prosecutor for respondent/State.

entities.text:
High Court Of Madhya Pradesh
 At Gwalior
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text:
Heard on IA No.6926/2024, first application under Section 389(1) Cr.P.C. for suspension of sentence and grant of bail moved on behalf of sole appellant-Mohar Singh Kushwaha.
Present appellant stands convicted under Section 376(2)(N) of IPC and sentenced to undergo Life Imprisonment with fine of Rs.2000/- & under Section 506(2) of IPC and sentenced to undergo 1 year's R.I. with fine of Rs.500/- vide judgment of conviction and order of sentence dated 29/11/2023 passed by Special Judge (POCSO Act), Morena, District Morena in Special Case No.36/2018.

entities.text: Special Judge (POCSO Act), Morena, District Morena
entities.label: COURT

sentences.text: As transpired during the course of hearing that the present appellant so far has undergone incarceration of 6 years.

A s per prosecution story, on 9/2/2018, complainant/prosecutrix (PW-1) along with his father (PW-2), mother and his brother-in-law reached to Police Station Bagchini and gave a written complaint (Ex.P/1) to the effect that present appellant Mohar Singh Kushwaha S/o Kedar Singh Kushwaha is the resident of her village and was already married.

About 5-6 months ago, when she was going alone in the evening at around 6:00 O'clock to give food to her father at the farm, present appellant Mohar Singh closed her mouth in the farm of one Bablu Sikarwar and placed a sickle on his neck.
He forced her into the field and committed rape upon her.
Thereafter, threatened her that if she told anyone, he will kill his father and his family.
This way, whenever, he find her alone, he committed rape upon her.
She was always in fear that he might kill her father and brothers.
As a result of which, she got pregnant of about 5 months.
She started vomiting and feeling dizzy.

Then,
he told the whole things to her family members.
On the basis of aforesaid, FIR was lodged against the present appellant.
Investigation was set in motion.
Her statements under Sections 161 & 164 of Cr.P.C. were recorded.

1 formalities, challan was filed.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: The Sessions Court on appreciation of evidence placed on record convicted and sentenced the present appellant as mentioned above.

Learned counsel for the appellant while taking exception to the impugned judgment of conviction and order of sentence submits that the Sessions Court has not appreciated the evidence placed on record in correct perspective.
The judgment suffers from surmises and conjectures.
It is submitted by learned counsel for appellant that there is delay of 6 months in lodging of FIR.
Appellant and prosecutrix are well known to each other and in fact, it is a matter of consent.
It is further submitted that determination of age of prosecutrix is doubtful, therefore, it is not proved that prosecutrix was minor at the time of alleged incident.
Besides, so far appellant has suffered incarceration of 6 years.
Under such circumstances, appellant prays for suspension of sentence and grant of bail on such terms and conditions this Court deem fit and proper.

Per contra, learned Public Prosecutor, appearing on behalf of the respondent/State, while supporting the judgment impugned submits that no exception can be taken in the matter of suspension of sentence and grant of bail as admittedly the prosecutrix was minor aged about 17 years and 1 month at the time of occurrence of incident.
That apart, the DNA report is positive.
Hence, he prays for dismissal of the instant application.

Up o n hearing learned counsel for the parties, though this Court refrains from commenting upon rival contentions so advanced touching merits of the case, but regard being had to the fact that during trial, appellant remain on bail and did not misuse the liberty granted to him coupled with the fact that appellant has suffered incarceration of 6 years and that the appeal being of the year 2022 is not likely to be decided in near future, in the obtaining facts and circumstances of the case, we are of the view that present appellant is entitled to the benefit of suspension of sentence and grant of bail.

Accordingly, I.A. No.6926 of 2024 stands allowed and it is directed that the jail sentence of appellant-Mohar Singh Kushwaha shall remain suspended during pendency of the present appeal and he shall be released on bail subject to verification of the factum of depositing the fine amount and on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs.2,00,000/- (Rupees Two Lacs only) with one solvent surety in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Trial Court.

Appellant is directed to appear before the Registry of this Court first on 26.07.2024 and thereafter,
on other subsequent dates as may be fixed in this behalf.
Accordingly, the said IA stands allowed and disposed of.
Observations on facts, if any, are only for the purpose of deciding the instant I.A. and shall have no bearing on the merits of the appeal.
Certified copy as per rules.

(ROHIT ARYA) 
 JUDGE   (Dubey)
